name: smoke-separate
description: Interner tables under G1: does keeping the table out of humongous regions (no old-to-young stores per insert, no card scanning) make a compile-shaped workload faster? One op is one simulated compile (5M lookups, ~3.7 GB allocated, ~200 MB live), compiles back to back, G1, 8 GB heap, Graal 25.4.4.
One fork per table and round.

variantDescriptions.chained-weak: today's design, after dotc's `WeakHashSet`: one bucket array of weak `Entry` chains; humongous past 512K buckets
variantDescriptions.chained-strong: the same chains with strong entries
variantDescriptions.chunked-weak: retronym/scala3#117: open addressing over 64K-slot chunks (256 KB), weak via a slim `WeakReference` carrying the hash
variantDescriptions.chunked-strong: the same chunks holding elements directly
